definition: See Speculative Decoding — an inference technique using a fast draft model to propose tokens later verified by the target model.
details: The term is sometimes used interchangeably with speculative decoding in discussions of LLM serving infrastructure optimization.

explainer.lead: A term used in LLM serving infrastructure discussions to refer to the technique of having a fast draft model propose tokens that the target model later verifies. It is sometimes used interchangeably with speculative decoding.

tiers.eli5: Think of it as the fast helper making guesses ahead that the main model then approves.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers encounter the term when reading about serving infrastructure optimization and should map it to the draft-then-verify scheme. The pitfall is assuming it denotes a different mechanism from speculative decoding.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined by reference: speculative execution in LLM serving is the same draft-propose, target-verify technique as speculative decoding. Limit: it is a naming variant rather than a distinct method.

explainer.example: A serving blog describes cutting latency via speculative execution, meaning a draft model proposing tokens verified by the target model.
